rows.whatChanged:
One change, in one function, in one file.

THE SPLITTER. renderComposedPdf in scripts/build-census-v1-rcap-tx-custom-pleading.mjs defined its own splitToken that accumulated CHARACTERS and cut at whichever glyph first reached the 468pt margin. It is deleted. In its place the builder imports the shared separator-aware splitter, createTokenSplitter({ fits: fitsByFontMetrics(font, fontSize, maxWidth) }) from scripts/rcap-custom-pleading/split-token.mjs, built from this builder's own font metrics (Times-Roman 11pt) and its own column width (612 - 2*72 = 468pt). A route key too long for the column now breaks only at one of its own separators - after a colon, underscore, slash, dot or hyphen - so the broken line ends on the separator and announces itself as continuing. The call site in wrap() is unchanged; the same local name is now bound to the shared splitter.

THE ASSERTION. assert.equal(splitToken.hardSplits, 0, ...) runs after every composed document is laid out. A future route key with no separator to break on now FAILS THE BUILD instead of shipping chopped. hardSplits is zero on both fixtures today, which is why the build completes.

WHAT PAGE 16 SHIPPED BEFORE, READ OFF THE DELIVERED BYTES: three keys chopped mid-word in BOTH fixtures - '...-after-the-limi' / 'tations-period', '...-after-the-limit' / 'ations-period', '...-innocence-reli' / 'ef'. AFTER: the same three break as '...-after-the-' / 'limitations-period', '...-after-the-' / 'limitations-period' and '...-actual-innocence-' / 'relief'. All nine route keys reconstruct from the delivered text of both fixtures, 9 of 9, and the page's widest measured token falls from 467.66pt to 459.99pt.
